prompt: A company wants the accounts of its five executives protected so that tenant-wide Helpdesk Administrators and User Administrators cannot reset their passwords or change their properties. A small executive support team must still be able to manage those accounts. The company does not want to remove any existing tenant-level role assignments. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create an administrative unit with dynamic membership for the executives and assign the executive support team the User Administrator role scoped to it
Place the executive accounts in a restricted management administrative unit and assign the support team roles scoped to it
Require approval in Privileged Identity Management for every activation of the Helpdesk Administrator and User Administrator roles
Create a custom role without password reset permissions and assign it to the executive support team at tenant scope

explanation: Objects in a restricted management administrative unit can be modified only by administrators who hold a role explicitly scoped to that unit, so tenant-scoped Helpdesk and User Administrators are blocked without changing their assignments. A regular administrative unit with dynamic membership only adds scoped administrators; tenant-scoped administrators keep full control. PIM approval only gates role activation and still lets activated administrators reset executive passwords. A tenant-scoped custom role for the support team does nothing to stop the other administrators.

prompt: An administrator created an administrative unit named Finance last month and assigned scoped administrators to it. Security now asks that the Finance unit be converted so that even tenant-level Global Administrators cannot modify its members without a scoped assignment. What must the administrator do?

options.text: Edit the Finance administrative unit properties, change Restricted management administrative unit from No to Yes, and save
Change the membership type of the Finance administrative unit from Assigned to Dynamic
Create a new restricted management administrative unit and move the members and scoped roles to it
Mark the Finance administrative unit as role-assignable and nest it inside a role-assignable group

explanation: The restricted management setting can only be applied when an administrative unit is created and cannot be changed afterwards, so a new unit must be created and the members and scoped role assignments moved to it. Editing the existing unit's properties is not possible for this setting. Changing to dynamic membership affects how members are added, not who can manage them. Administrative units cannot be made role-assignable or nested inside groups.

prompt: A developer must be able to rotate the client secrets and certificates of one specific app registration, and nothing else in the tenant. The tenant has Microsoft Entra ID P1. Which approach grants the least privilege?

options.text: Assign the developer the Cloud Application Administrator role at tenant scope so they can manage the app's secrets
Add the developer as an owner of the app registration from the Owners page of that registration
Assign the developer the Application Developer role at tenant scope
A custom role with only the application credentials update permission, scoped to that app registration

explanation: A custom Microsoft Entra role with only the credentials update permission, assigned at the scope of a single app registration, grants exactly the needed capability. Cloud Application Administrator at tenant scope can manage every application in the tenant. Owners of an app registration can change all of its settings, not just its credentials. Application Developer lets a user create new app registrations and does not grant management of an existing one they do not own.

prompt: A company with offices in France and Germany wants users whose browser language is French to see French sign-in page text and a different background image, while all other users keep the default branding. What should the administrator configure in Company branding?

options.text: A French browser-language customization alongside the default sign-in experience
A second custom domain for French users, with company branding scoped to that domain
A Conditional Access policy that targets French locations with a custom terms of use
An administrative unit for French users with its own branding assigned to it

explanation: Company branding supports a default sign-in experience plus language-specific customizations that are shown based on the browser language. Branding is not scoped per custom domain. Terms of use in Conditional Access show an agreement, not sign-in page branding. Administrative units delegate administration and do not carry their own branding.

prompt: An administrator added the custom domain contoso.com to Microsoft Entra ID, and it shows as Unverified. The administrator does not have permission to change the domain's MX records. What must happen before users can be given user principal names ending in @contoso.com?

options.text: Create a CNAME record named autodiscover that points to autodiscover.outlook.com, then select Verify
Add the TXT verification record shown in the admin center at the DNS host, then select Verify
Add an SPF TXT record that includes spf.protection.outlook.com, then select Verify
Make contoso.com the primary domain of the tenant so it is verified automatically

explanation: Domain ownership is proven by adding the TXT (or MX) verification record that Microsoft Entra ID displays to the public DNS zone and then running verification; the TXT option avoids touching mail routing. The autodiscover CNAME is used by Exchange Online clients and does not prove ownership. An SPF record authorises mail senders and is not the verification record. An unverified domain cannot be set as the primary domain.

prompt: A Global Administrator creates an attribute set named Engineering, but when they try to assign values of its custom security attribute CostCenter to users, the option is unavailable. What is the least privileged way for this administrator to assign the attribute values?

options.text: Assign the Attribute Definition Administrator role for the Engineering attribute set
Assign the User Administrator role at tenant scope
Assign the Attribute Assignment Administrator role
Assign the Privileged Role Administrator role at tenant scope

explanation: Global Administrator and other admin roles do not have permission to read, define or assign custom security attributes by default; Attribute Assignment Administrator is the minimum role for assigning values, and it can be scoped to an attribute set. Attribute Definition Administrator manages the attribute definitions but does not assign values to objects. User Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator have no custom security attribute permissions; Privileged Role Administrator could only grant the role.

prompt: HR wants to store each employee's salary band on their Microsoft Entra user object. Only a delegated group of HR administrators should be able to read or change the value; other administrators and applications that can read user objects must not see it. What should the administrator use?

options.text: A directory extension attribute registered on an HR application and populated through Microsoft Graph
One of the onPremisesExtensionAttributes synchronized from the employee's Active Directory account
A schema extension registered through Microsoft Graph
A custom security attribute in a dedicated attribute set with HR administrators assigned to that set

explanation: Custom security attributes have their own read and write permissions controlled through dedicated roles that can be scoped to an attribute set, so the value is hidden from anyone without those roles. Directory extensions, schema extensions and the onPremises extension attributes are readable by anyone with permission to read the user object, so they are not suitable for sensitive data.

prompt: An administrator must write a script that runs weekly, reads new hires from a CSV file, and creates cloud-only Microsoft Entra users. The script must use a currently supported PowerShell module. Which approach should the administrator use?

options.text: Import-Csv with the New-MgUser cmdlet from the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK
Import-Csv with the New-AzureADUser cmdlet from the AzureAD PowerShell module for Microsoft Entra ID
Import-Csv with the New-MsolUser cmdlet from the MSOnline module
Import-Csv with the New-ADUser cmdlet from the ActiveDirectory module

explanation: The Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK is the supported module for managing Microsoft Entra objects, and New-MgUser creates cloud users. The AzureAD and MSOnline modules are retired. New-ADUser creates accounts in on-premises Active Directory, not cloud-only Microsoft Entra users.

prompt: Employees want to use their personally owned Windows laptops to access Microsoft 365 with their work accounts. The devices must appear in Microsoft Entra ID so Conditional Access can evaluate them, but the company must not take ownership of the devices or require users to sign in to Windows with their work accounts. What should the administrator plan for?

options.text: Microsoft Entra join
Microsoft Entra hybrid join
Microsoft Entra registration
Windows Autopilot deployment

explanation: Microsoft Entra registered devices are personal devices where users add a work account and keep signing in with a local or personal account, which fits bring-your-own-device. Microsoft Entra join is for organisation-owned devices where users sign in to Windows with their work account. Hybrid join requires the device to be joined to on-premises Active Directory. Autopilot provisions organisation-owned devices, typically into Microsoft Entra join.

prompt: A company wants every user whose department attribute is Sales to receive a Microsoft 365 E5 license automatically, including future hires, and to lose it automatically if they move to another department. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An administrative unit with a dynamic membership rule for Sales and the license assigned to the administrative unit
A security group with a dynamic membership rule of (user.department -eq "Sales") and the license assigned to the group
A weekly bulk operation that assigns licenses to users exported from a filtered Sales user list
A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership that Sales managers maintain, with the license assigned to the group

explanation: Group-based licensing on a dynamic security group adds and removes licenses as users enter and leave the group based on the department attribute. Licenses cannot be assigned to administrative units. A weekly bulk operation is manual, leaves gaps between runs and does not remove licenses. An assigned-membership group depends on managers updating it and is not automatic.

prompt: Contoso owns two Microsoft Entra tenants and wants users from its HQ tenant to be created automatically as users in its Subsidiary tenant. The administrator configures a cross-tenant synchronization job in the HQ tenant, but provisioning fails. What must be configured in the Subsidiary tenant?

options.text: Outbound cross-tenant access settings for HQ with B2B collaboration allowed for all users and applications
A cross-tenant synchronization job that pulls users from the HQ tenant
An external collaboration setting that allows member users to invite guests
Inbound cross-tenant access settings for HQ with Allow user synchronization into this tenant selected

explanation: Cross-tenant synchronization is a push from the source tenant, and the target tenant must allow it through the inbound Allow user synchronization into this tenant setting in its cross-tenant access settings for the source organisation. Outbound settings in the target control its own users going elsewhere. There is no pull-based sync job in the target tenant. Guest invitation settings do not govern synchronization.

prompt: Fabrikam collaborates with a partner that also uses Microsoft Entra ID. Partner users already complete MFA in their home tenant, and Fabrikam's Conditional Access policy requiring MFA forces them to register and perform MFA again in Fabrikam. Fabrikam wants to accept the partner's MFA for this partner only. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: In Fabrikam's inbound cross-tenant access settings for the partner organisation, enable Trust multifactor authentication from Microsoft Entra tenants
In Fabrikam's outbound cross-tenant access settings for the partner organisation, enable Trust multifactor authentication from Microsoft Entra tenants
In External collaboration settings, add the partner domain to the allow list
Exclude all guest and external users from the Conditional Access policy that requires MFA

explanation: Trust settings are part of the inbound cross-tenant access settings, configured per organisation, and let the resource tenant accept MFA claims from the user's home tenant. Trust settings are not part of outbound settings. The external collaboration allow list only controls which domains can be invited. Excluding external users removes the MFA requirement entirely instead of trusting the partner's MFA.

prompt: Two companies want users in each organisation to join Microsoft Teams shared channels hosted by the other, without creating guest accounts in either directory. What must both organisations configure?

options.text: B2B collaboration inbound and outbound settings in cross-tenant access settings
Cross-tenant synchronization jobs in both directions
B2B direct connect inbound and outbound settings for each other in cross-tenant access settings
A connected organization for each other in entitlement management, with an access package for the Teams channels

explanation: Teams shared channels use B2B direct connect, which does not create user objects in the resource tenant and must be enabled mutually through inbound and outbound cross-tenant access settings. B2B collaboration creates guest accounts. Cross-tenant synchronization creates user objects in the target tenant. Connected organizations let external users request access packages, which also results in guest accounts.

prompt: A partner organisation authenticates its users with a third-party identity provider that supports SAML 2.0 and does not use Microsoft Entra ID. The company wants partner guests to sign in with their existing partner credentials. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Cross-tenant access settings for the partner's domain
A SAML/WS-Fed identity provider in External Identities configured for the partner's domain
Email one-time passcode for guest users
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with an additional connector that reads the partner's user directory

explanation: SAML/WS-Fed identity provider federation lets guests from a partner domain authenticate against the partner's own SAML 2.0 or WS-Fed identity provider. Cross-tenant access settings apply only to other Microsoft Entra organisations. Email one-time passcode signs users in with a code sent to their email, not with their partner credentials. Connect Sync synchronizes on-premises Active Directory and is not used for partner sign-in.

prompt: Legal requires that guest invitations can be sent only to users at three approved partner domains. Invitations to any other domain must fail. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Guest user access restrictions set to the most restrictive level
Guest invite settings set so that only users assigned to specific admin roles can invite
A Conditional Access policy that blocks sign-in for guest users whose home domain is not one of the three partners
Collaboration restrictions in External collaboration settings set to allow invitations only to the specified domains

explanation: The collaboration restrictions in External collaboration settings support an allow list of domains, so invitations to unlisted domains are blocked. Guest user access restrictions control what guests can see in the directory. Guest invite settings control who can send invitations, not to which domains. A Conditional Access policy acts at sign-in and would not stop the invitations from being created.

prompt: A company acquires another business that has its own Active Directory forest. There is no network connectivity or trust between the acquired forest and the existing Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server, and the company wants a lightweight, highly available way to synchronize the acquired users into its tenant. What should the administrator deploy?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync provisioning agents on servers in the acquired forest
Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication agents in the acquired forest
Microsoft Entra Connect Health agents in the acquired forest
An AD FS farm in the acquired forest, federated with the tenant through a Web Application Proxy

explanation: Cloud Sync uses lightweight provisioning agents that need only outbound connectivity, supports multiple disconnected forests, and supports several active agents for high availability. Pass-through authentication agents validate passwords but do not create user objects. Connect Health agents only monitor. AD FS handles authentication for existing users and does not synchronize identities.

prompt: A company uses password hash synchronization with Seamless single sign-on. A security review notes that the Kerberos decryption key of the AZUREADSSO computer account has not changed since deployment two years ago. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Reset the password of the AZUREADSSO account in Active Directory Users and Computers
Disable and re-enable password hash synchronization in Microsoft Entra Connect
Run Update-AzureADSSOForest once for each forest where Seamless SSO is enabled, and repeat at least every 30 days
Delete the AZUREADSSO computer account and let Microsoft Entra Connect re-create it with a new key at the next sync cycle

explanation: Microsoft recommends rolling over the AZUREADSSO Kerberos decryption key at least every 30 days with Update-AzureADSSOForest, run once per forest, which updates the key both on-premises and in Microsoft Entra ID. Resetting the password locally does not update the key held in Microsoft Entra ID and breaks SSO. Toggling password hash synchronization does not touch the SSO account. Deleting the account breaks Seamless SSO and it is not re-created by a sync cycle.

prompt: A company uses pass-through authentication with a single authentication agent installed on the Microsoft Entra Connect server. Users could not sign in while that server was being patched. What should the administrator do to prevent this?

options.text: Configure a second Microsoft Entra Connect server in staging mode
Install additional standalone pass-through authentication agents on other domain-joined servers
Open inbound TCP 443 from the internet to the Microsoft Entra Connect server
Enable Seamless single sign-on so that domain-joined users can still sign in while the agent is offline

explanation: Pass-through authentication load-balances sign-in requests across all registered agents, so installing extra agents on other servers provides high availability. A staging-mode Connect server does not process pass-through sign-ins. The agents only make outbound connections, so inbound ports are not needed. Seamless SSO still relies on Microsoft Entra ID being able to validate the user and does not replace the agent for password sign-ins.

prompt: A company plans to move from AD FS federation to cloud authentication with password hash synchronization. Before converting the federated domain, it wants to test cloud authentication with a pilot group of users while everyone else keeps signing in through AD FS. What should the administrator use?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Connect staging mode on a second server configured for the pilot users
A Conditional Access policy that targets the pilot group and requires cloud MFA at sign-in
Staged Rollout with the pilot group enabled for password hash synchronization
Microsoft Entra Connect Health for AD FS

explanation: Staged Rollout lets selected groups use cloud authentication such as password hash synchronization while the domain stays federated for everyone else. Staging mode is for a standby sync server and does not change how users authenticate. Conditional Access applies controls after authentication and cannot redirect where authentication happens. Connect Health monitors AD FS but does not migrate users.

prompt: A company keeps AD FS for a few legacy applications and wants reports in the Microsoft Entra admin center showing AD FS failed sign-ins by user and the IP addresses generating repeated bad-password attempts against AD FS. What should the administrator deploy?

options.text: Diagnostic settings that send Microsoft Entra sign-in logs to a Log Analytics workspace
Microsoft Entra Connect Health for sync, which installs with Microsoft Entra Connect
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync provisioning agents on the AD FS servers
Connect Health for AD FS agents on the AD FS and Web Application Proxy servers

explanation: Connect Health for AD FS agents collect AD FS usage, performance and alert data and provide reports such as bad password attempts and the risky IP report. Microsoft Entra sign-in logs do not contain sign-ins that AD FS processes itself. Connect Health for sync monitors the synchronization engine, not AD FS. Cloud Sync agents synchronize identities and do not monitor AD FS.

prompt: The Temporary Access Pass method is enabled in the Authentication methods policy for a group named Onboarding. A helpdesk technician with the Authentication Administrator role creates a Temporary Access Pass for a new employee, but at sign-in the employee is only prompted for a password. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The pass was created with one-time use enabled
The employee is not a member of the Onboarding group targeted by the Temporary Access Pass policy
Authentication Administrators cannot create a Temporary Access Pass for member users; only Privileged Authentication Administrators can
The employee has not yet registered Microsoft Authenticator

explanation: A Temporary Access Pass can be created for any user, but only users included in the Temporary Access Pass authentication methods policy can sign in with it, so the employee must be in the targeted group. One-time use limits how often the pass works but does not hide the prompt. Authentication Administrators can create passes for member users. A Temporary Access Pass is designed for users with no other methods, so Authenticator is not required.

prompt: A Global Administrator lost the only device that held their passkey and needs a Temporary Access Pass to register a new one. Which role, with the least privilege, can create the Temporary Access Pass for this account?

options.text: Authentication Administrator
Authentication Policy Administrator
Helpdesk Administrator
Privileged Authentication Administrator

explanation: Privileged Authentication Administrators can create, view and delete a Temporary Access Pass for administrators as well as members. Authentication Administrators can do so only for non-admin members. Authentication Policy Administrators configure the method policy but do not issue passes to users. Helpdesk Administrator does not manage authentication methods such as Temporary Access Pass.

prompt: Users on Microsoft Entra hybrid joined Windows 11 devices will sign in with FIDO2 security keys. They must get single sign-on to on-premises file shares that use Kerberos, without deploying a PKI. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a Microsoft Entra Kerberos server object in each domain with Set-AzureADKerberosServer
Run Update-AzureADSSOForest to configure the AZUREADSSO computer account so Seamless SSO issues Kerberos tickets
Deploy Windows Hello for Business with the certificate trust model
Switch the tenant from password hash synchronization to pass-through authentication

explanation: Microsoft Entra Kerberos lets Microsoft Entra ID issue partial Kerberos TGTs for the on-premises domain once a Kerberos server object is created with Set-AzureADKerberosServer, giving security key users SSO to Active Directory resources. Update-AzureADSSOForest rolls the Seamless SSO key and has nothing to do with security key sign-in. Certificate trust needs a PKI, which the scenario rules out. Pass-through authentication validates passwords and does not provide Kerberos tickets for security key sign-in.

prompt: A user's cloud-only account was used by an attacker. The administrator must stop the account signing in again and invalidate the refresh tokens and session cookies already issued to the attacker. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Remove all licenses from the user and require the user to re-register MFA
Create a Conditional Access policy for the user with a sign-in frequency of one hour
Block sign-in for the account and revoke its sessions
Delete the user's registered authentication methods and leave the account enabled

explanation: Blocking sign-in prevents new authentication, and revoking sessions invalidates the refresh tokens and session cookies already issued so the attacker must reauthenticate and is then blocked. Removing licenses does not stop sign-in, and re-registering MFA does not revoke tokens. A one-hour sign-in frequency still leaves the existing session usable and the account able to sign in. Deleting authentication methods leaves the account enabled and does not invalidate tokens.

prompt: A company has added its product names to the custom banned password list in Microsoft Entra Password Protection. It now wants the same list to block those words when users change passwords on-premises with Ctrl+Alt+Del on domain-joined computers. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Enable password writeback in Microsoft Entra Connect
Deploy the Password Protection proxy service and DC agents, and set the mode to Enforced
Create a fine-grained password policy in Active Directory that contains the product names as prohibited values
Install the Password Protection DC agent and leave the on-premises mode set to Audit

explanation: On-premises enforcement requires the proxy service, which fetches the policy from Microsoft Entra ID, and the DC agent on domain controllers, with the mode set to Enforced so non-compliant passwords are rejected. Password writeback sends cloud password resets to Active Directory and does not evaluate on-premises changes. Fine-grained password policies control length and complexity, not banned words. Audit mode only logs violations.

prompt: A company requires that administrators signing in to the Azure portal use only a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, or certificate-based authentication. SMS and Authenticator push approvals must not satisfy the requirement. Which grant control should the Conditional Access policy use?

options.text: Require multifactor authentication for the selected administrator roles
Require device to be marked as compliant
Require authentication strength: Phishing-resistant MFA
Require approved client app

explanation: Authentication strengths specify which method combinations satisfy the policy, and the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength allows only methods such as passkeys, Windows Hello for Business and certificate-based authentication. Require multifactor authentication accepts any registered MFA method, including SMS. Device compliance checks the device, not the sign-in method. Require approved client app applies to mobile apps.

prompt: Security wants anyone who creates, updates or deletes a Conditional Access policy to complete phishing-resistant MFA at the moment they make the change, regardless of which role grants them the permission. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy targeting the Microsoft Admin Portals app that requires phishing-resistant MFA at sign-in
A PIM setting that requires a Conditional Access authentication context when the Conditional Access Administrator role is activated
A custom role without Conditional Access permissions assigned to all administrators
Protected actions for the Conditional Access permissions, using an authentication context that requires phishing-resistant MFA

explanation: Protected actions assign an authentication context to specific permissions, such as creating or deleting Conditional Access policies, so the linked policy is enforced when the action is attempted no matter how the permission was granted. A policy on Microsoft Admin Portals applies at sign-in, not at the time of the change. A PIM activation requirement covers only that one role and only at activation. Removing permissions through a custom role changes authorisation instead of adding a step-up requirement.

prompt: Users can open most SharePoint Online sites after a normal sign-in, but the company wants an extra step-up requirement, compliant device plus MFA, only when users open the site that holds merger documents. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: An authentication context requiring MFA and a compliant device, linked to the merger site's sensitivity label
A Conditional Access policy targeting Office 365 that requires MFA and a compliant device for every user
App-enforced restrictions for SharePoint Online in a Conditional Access session control
A named location for the merger team's office and a Conditional Access policy that blocks all other locations

explanation: Authentication context lets a Conditional Access policy apply to a specific resource inside an app, such as a SharePoint site linked through a sensitivity label, so step-up happens only for that site. A policy targeting Office 365 would apply to every site and service. App-enforced restrictions limit unmanaged-device sessions but do not require MFA for one site. A location block does not require a compliant device or MFA.

prompt: When an employee is terminated, the administrator disables the account, but the employee can keep reading mail in Exchange Online until the access token expires. The company wants Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams to respond to account disablement and password resets in near real time. Which capability addresses this?

options.text: A sign-in frequency session control of one hour
Continuous access evaluation
Persistent browser session set to Never persistent
Token protection for sign-in sessions

explanation: Continuous access evaluation lets CAE-capable services such as Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Teams receive critical events like account disablement and password resets and reject tokens in near real time. Sign-in frequency still allows the current token to be used until reauthentication is due. Persistent browser session controls browser cookies, not access tokens already in use. Token protection binds tokens to a device to stop replay but does not react to account disablement.

prompt: An administrator built a new Conditional Access policy that blocks access from outside named locations. Before enforcing it, they want to see which users it would affect and to check how it would apply to one user signing in from a specific IP address. Which two actions should the administrator take?

options.text: Set the policy to Report-only and review the results in the sign-in logs
Enable security defaults while the policy is tested
Use the What If tool with the user, app and IP address
Turn the policy On for all users and monitor helpdesk tickets for a week
Exclude all users from the policy and add a sign-in frequency control

explanation: Report-only mode evaluates the policy at each sign-in and records the result without enforcing it, and the What If tool shows which policies would apply for a chosen user, app and IP address. Security defaults cannot be enabled while Conditional Access policies are in use and do not test a policy. Turning the policy on enforces it and risks lockout. Excluding everyone means the policy is never evaluated for anyone.

prompt: ID Protection reports a Leaked Credentials detection on a single-tenant service principal used by a nightly integration job. The administrator has confirmed the exposure. What should the administrator do to remediate it?

options.text: Require the service principal to perform a secure password change through a user risk Conditional Access policy
Reset MFA for the service principal and require it to register again
Add the service principal to a sign-in risk Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication
Add a new certificate credential, remove the compromised secrets and rotate Key Vault secrets it can read

explanation: Remediating a compromised workload identity means replacing its credentials, preferably with an X.509 certificate, removing the compromised credentials and rotating secrets it had access to. User risk and password change policies apply to users, not service principals. Workload identities cannot perform MFA, so MFA reset and MFA requirements do not apply.

prompt: A company with Workload Identities Premium licenses wants to block sign-ins automatically whenever ID Protection marks a workload identity as high risk. For which identity can the administrator create this risk-based Conditional Access policy?

options.text: A system-assigned managed identity on an Azure virtual machine
A single-tenant service principal registered in the company's tenant
A multitenant SaaS application published by a third party
A user account used as a service account

explanation: Conditional Access for workload identities, including the service principal risk condition, applies to single-tenant service principals registered in the tenant. Managed identities and multitenant or third-party SaaS applications are out of scope. A user account is not a workload identity and would be covered by user risk policies instead.

prompt: A company with Microsoft Entra ID P2 wants users to complete MFA whenever ID Protection evaluates a sign-in as medium or high risk, while low-risk sign-ins proceed normally. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy with the sign-in risk condition set to High and Medium and the grant control set to require MFA
A Conditional Access policy with the user risk condition set to High and Medium and the grant control set to require MFA and password change
A Conditional Access policy that blocks all locations except trusted named locations
The ID Protection multifactor authentication registration policy for all users

explanation: Sign-in risk reflects the probability that a particular authentication request is not authorised by the account owner, so a sign-in risk policy requiring MFA challenges only the risky sign-ins. User risk measures the likelihood the account itself is compromised and is the wrong signal here. A location block does not use risk at all. The MFA registration policy makes users register MFA but does not challenge risky sign-ins.

prompt: Many users still rely on SMS for MFA. The company wants users to be prompted during sign-in to set up Microsoft Authenticator, with a limited number of chances to postpone. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: The ID Protection multifactor authentication registration policy assigned to all users
The self-service password reset registration requirement
A registration campaign in the Authentication methods settings that targets Microsoft Authenticator
A Conditional Access policy that requires multifactor authentication for all cloud apps and all users

explanation: A registration campaign nudges targeted users at sign-in to set up Microsoft Authenticator and lets administrators control how many times they can snooze the prompt. The ID Protection MFA registration policy requires users to register MFA but does not specifically move them to Authenticator. The SSPR registration requirement concerns password reset methods. Requiring MFA lets users keep using SMS.

prompt: ID Protection flags a user as high risk after an atypical travel detection. The administrator confirms with the user that they were travelling and that the sign-ins were legitimate. The administrator wants to clear the risk without forcing the user to change anything. What should the administrator do in the Risky users report?

options.text: Select Confirm user compromised
Select Reset password and require a change at next sign-in
Select Block user
Select Dismiss user risk

explanation: Dismiss user risk is used when the administrator determines the activity was legitimate, and it sets the user risk to none. Confirm user compromised raises the risk to high and is for real compromises. Resetting the password remediates risk but forces a change the scenario wants to avoid. Blocking the user prevents legitimate work.

prompt: An administrator must install the Global Secure Access client silently on 2,000 Microsoft Entra joined Windows 11 devices managed by Microsoft Intune. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Package the installer as an .intunewin file and deploy it as a required Win32 app
Enable the Microsoft traffic forwarding profile so that the client installs automatically on joined devices
Configure a remote network for each office so that devices download the client
Assign the Global Secure Access Administrator role to device users so they can install the client from the admin center

explanation: The client can be installed silently with the /quiet switch, and Intune deploys it as a Win32 app packaged with the Win32 Content Prep Tool. Enabling a traffic forwarding profile decides which traffic the client tunnels but does not install anything. Remote networks connect branch sites without a client and do not push software. Giving end users an admin role breaks least privilege and still requires manual installs.

prompt: With Microsoft Entra Internet Access, a company wants to block the Gambling web category for all users except the security research team. The Internet Access traffic forwarding profile is enabled. Which configuration enforces this?

options.text: A Conditional Access policy for Office 365 that uses the app-enforced restrictions session control and excludes the research team
A web content filtering policy in a security profile, applied by a Conditional Access policy that excludes the research team
A Defender for Cloud Apps session policy that blocks the Gambling category for every user except the research team
A default cross-tenant access setting that blocks outbound access from users to gambling domains

explanation: Web content filtering policies are grouped into security profiles, and Conditional Access delivers the profile to the chosen users through the Use Global Secure Access security profile session control on All internet resources with Global Secure Access. App-enforced restrictions concern SharePoint and Exchange sessions. Defender for Cloud Apps session policies act on sessions to apps routed through Conditional Access app control, not general web categories. Cross-tenant access settings govern collaboration with other Microsoft Entra tenants.

prompt: A company is replacing its VPN with Microsoft Entra Private Access. An on-premises HR application and an on-premises finance application must each have different Conditional Access requirements. Which configuration should the administrator use?

options.text: Quick Access with both application segments added and one Conditional Access policy assigned to Quick Access
A Microsoft Entra application proxy published URL for each application
A separate per-app access application for each app, each with its own Conditional Access policy
The Microsoft traffic forwarding profile with a Conditional Access policy for each application

explanation: Per-app access creates an enterprise application for each private app's segments, so each can be assigned users and targeted by its own Conditional Access policy, and it supports any TCP or UDP protocol. Quick Access is a single application for broad IP ranges and FQDNs, so both apps would share one policy. Application proxy publishes web applications only. The Microsoft traffic profile handles Microsoft 365 traffic, not private apps.

prompt: To use Microsoft Entra Private Access for applications in the company's datacenter, which component must the administrator install in the datacenter network?

options.text: The Global Secure Access client installed on each application server in the datacenter
A Microsoft Entra Connect Sync server in staging mode
An inbound firewall rule on TCP 443 and a reverse proxy server in the perimeter network
The Microsoft Entra private network connector on a server that can reach the apps

explanation: Private Access relies on private network connectors, installed on Windows Servers with line of sight to the applications, which make outbound connections to the service, so no inbound ports are needed. The client is installed on user devices, not application servers. Connect Sync synchronizes identities and has no role in traffic. An inbound rule and reverse proxy are what the connector model avoids.

prompt: To reduce data exfiltration, a company wants to stop users on corporate devices running the Global Secure Access client from signing in to other organisations' Microsoft Entra tenants or to personal Microsoft accounts, without deploying a proxy that injects headers. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Universal Tenant Restrictions enforcing a tenant restrictions v2 policy
Outbound B2B collaboration set to block in the default cross-tenant access settings for all external tenants
A web content filtering policy that blocks the login.microsoftonline.com FQDN
External collaboration settings that disable guest invitations

explanation: Universal Tenant Restrictions, delivered through the Microsoft traffic profile, add tenant restrictions v2 signalling to the traffic so the tenant restrictions v2 policy is enforced without a header-injecting proxy. Outbound B2B collaboration settings control which external tenants users can be invited into, but not personal accounts or tokens obtained in other tenants on corporate devices. Blocking the sign-in FQDN breaks sign-in to the company's own tenant. Guest invitation settings control inbound guests, not where users sign in.

prompt: An Azure Functions app must read secrets from one Azure Key Vault. The function is the only workload that needs this access, and developers must not store or rotate any credentials. When the function app is deleted, its identity should be removed automatically. Which identity should the administrator use?

options.text: A service principal with a client secret stored in the function's application settings
A system-assigned managed identity enabled on the function app
A dedicated cloud user account whose password is stored in Key Vault
A group managed service account

explanation: A system-assigned managed identity has no credentials for anyone to manage, is used only by the resource it is enabled on, and is deleted with that resource. A service principal with a client secret leaves a secret to store and rotate. A user account brings a password and interactive sign-in risk. Group managed service accounts are on-premises Active Directory accounts and cannot be used by an Azure function.

prompt: A web tier runs on virtual machines that are frequently deleted and rebuilt. Every VM needs the same access to an Azure SQL database, and the access must be granted before the VMs are created as part of the provisioning pipeline. Which identity type fits best?

options.text: A user-assigned managed identity assigned to each VM
A system-assigned managed identity enabled on each VM
A separate app registration with a certificate for each VM
A single cloud user account shared by all VMs

explanation: A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone resource with its own lifecycle, can be shared by many resources and can be granted access before the VMs exist, so permissions survive rebuilds. System-assigned identities are created and deleted with each VM, so access would have to be granted again after every rebuild. Per-VM app registrations add certificates to manage. A shared user account is a credential risk and not designed for workloads.

prompt: A Windows service runs on four on-premises member servers and must authenticate to an on-premises SQL Server with Active Directory credentials. Security requires that the account password is managed and rotated automatically and that the account can be used on all four servers. What should the administrator use?

options.text: A user-assigned managed identity
A standalone managed service account
A group managed service account
A Microsoft Entra service principal with a certificate

explanation: A group managed service account has its password managed by Active Directory and can be used on multiple servers. A standalone managed service account is limited to a single computer. Managed identities exist only for Azure resources. A Microsoft Entra service principal does not provide Active Directory authentication to an on-premises SQL Server.

prompt: A virtual machine has a system-assigned managed identity. Code on the VM must read blobs from a storage account by using that identity, without account keys or SAS tokens. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign the managed identity the Reader role on the storage account
Assign the managed identity the Application Administrator Microsoft Entra role
Store the storage account access key in an environment variable on the VM and read it from the code
Assign the managed identity the Storage Blob Data Reader role on the storage account or container

explanation: Access to blob data with Microsoft Entra authentication requires an Azure RBAC data-plane role such as Storage Blob Data Reader at the account or container scope. The Reader role covers only management-plane properties and does not grant blob data access. Microsoft Entra directory roles do not grant access to Azure resources. Using an access key defeats the purpose of a managed identity.

prompt: A deployment engineer already has the Virtual Machine Contributor role on a resource group. They need to attach an existing user-assigned managed identity to VMs in that resource group, but must not be able to create, change or delete managed identities. Which additional role should they be given on the identity?

options.text: Managed Identity Contributor
Managed Identity Operator
User Access Administrator
Owner

explanation: Managed Identity Operator allows a user to read and assign a user-assigned identity to resources without being able to create, update or delete it. Managed Identity Contributor can create, update and delete identities, which is more than needed. User Access Administrator manages role assignments, and Owner grants full control; both exceed the requirement.

prompt: A company wants remote users to reach an internal web-based timesheet application with Microsoft Entra pre-authentication and Conditional Access, without a VPN and without opening inbound firewall ports. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Publish the app with Microsoft Entra application proxy and a private network connector
Deploy an AD FS farm with Web Application Proxy servers in the perimeter network
Create an app registration for the timesheet app and add its internal URL as a redirect URI
Publish the timesheet app through a public load balancer and require MFA in Conditional Access

explanation: Application proxy publishes internal web apps through an external URL, uses Microsoft Entra pre-authentication so Conditional Access applies, and its connectors use only outbound connections. AD FS and Web Application Proxy need inbound access to the perimeter network and add infrastructure. An app registration with a redirect URI does not make an internal app reachable from the internet. A public load balancer requires opening inbound ports to the app.

prompt: A company has set user consent to Do not allow user consent. Users now see a message that they need admin approval and cannot ask for access to new apps. The company wants users to submit a justification that designated reviewers can approve or deny. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Permission classifications that mark common Microsoft Graph permissions as low impact for user consent
The admin consent workflow with designated users, groups or roles as reviewers
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA before consenting
App governance policies in Defender for Cloud Apps

explanation: The admin consent workflow lets users request access to apps they cannot consent to, with a justification, and routes the request to the designated reviewers. Permission classifications only matter when user consent is allowed for selected permissions. Conditional Access does not provide a consent request process. App governance monitors and alerts on OAuth apps but does not handle consent requests.

prompt: To reduce consent phishing risk, a company wants users to be able to consent only to apps from verified publishers or apps registered in its own tenant, and only for permissions the company considers low risk. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Set user consent to Allow user consent for apps, and enable the admin consent workflow
Set user consent to Do not allow user consent, and grant tenant-wide admin consent for every requested app
Allow consent for verified publishers for selected permissions, and classify low-impact permissions
Set Users can register applications to No in the user settings

explanation: The verified publishers setting restricts user consent to apps from verified publishers or registered in the tenant, and only for permissions classified as low impact, so the classification step is required. Allow user consent for apps lets users consent to any permission that does not need admin consent, from any publisher. Disabling user consent and granting admin consent for every app removes the self-service the company wants. Blocking app registration does not control consent to existing multitenant apps.

prompt: A team member needs to create and manage enterprise applications and app registrations, including SSO and user assignment, across the tenant. They must not be able to manage application proxy settings. Which built-in role grants the least privilege?

options.text: Application Administrator
Application Developer
Global Administrator
Cloud Application Administrator

explanation: Cloud Application Administrator has the same permissions as Application Administrator except for managing application proxy. Application Administrator includes application proxy management, which the scenario excludes. Application Developer can only create registrations and does not manage all apps. Global Administrator is far more than needed.

prompt: Sales users have about 15 assigned applications in My Apps. The sales director wants the five CRM and quoting apps grouped together under a Sales tools heading for Sales users only. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Create a My Apps collection containing the five apps and assign it to the Sales group
Create an administrative unit containing the five apps and assign it to the Sales group
Add an app role named Sales tools to each of the five apps
Create an access package containing the five apps for the Sales group

explanation: Collections group applications into named sections in My Apps and can be assigned to specific users or groups. Administrative units delegate administration and do not change the My Apps layout. App roles control authorisation within an app, not how apps are presented. Access packages grant access through requests and do not create a section in My Apps.

prompt: Developers are registering a new app that customers will sign in to with either their work account from any Microsoft Entra organisation or a personal Microsoft account such as Outlook.com. Which supported account type should they select?

options.text: Accounts in this organizational directory only
Accounts in any organizational directory
Personal Microsoft accounts only
Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts

explanation: The combined multitenant and personal accounts option allows sign-in from any Microsoft Entra organisation and from personal Microsoft accounts. Accounts in this organizational directory only is single tenant. Accounts in any organizational directory excludes personal accounts. Personal Microsoft accounts only excludes work and school accounts.

prompt: A React single-page application signs users in with MSAL.js by using the authorization code flow with PKCE. How should the redirect URI be configured on the app registration?

options.text: Add it under the Web platform and enable ID tokens for the implicit grant
Add it under the Single-page application platform
Add it under the Mobile and desktop applications platform
Add it as an Application ID URI under Expose an API

explanation: The Single-page application platform marks the redirect URI as allowing the authorization code flow with PKCE and cross-origin token redemption from the browser. The Web platform is for server-side apps that can keep a secret, and the implicit grant is the older flow this design avoids. Mobile and desktop is for native clients. The Application ID URI identifies an API and is not a redirect URI.

prompt: A background service with no signed-in user must read mail from every mailbox in the tenant through Microsoft Graph. How should the API permission be configured?

options.text: Add the Mail.Read delegated permission and let each user consent
Add the Mail.Read application permission and grant admin consent for the tenant
Add the Mail.Read delegated permission and grant admin consent for the tenant
Add the User.Read delegated permission and assign the service the Exchange Administrator role

explanation: An app that runs without a signed-in user uses application permissions, and application permissions always require admin consent. Delegated permissions act on behalf of a signed-in user, so they do not work for a daemon, even with admin consent. User.Read only reads the signed-in user's profile, and a directory role does not grant Graph mail access.

prompt: A line-of-business app must decide whether a signed-in user is an Approver or a Viewer. The developers want the decision to come from a claim in the token, and administrators want to manage who has each role from the enterprise application. What should be configured?

options.text: Add a groups claim to the token, create a security group for each role, and map the group IDs in code
Create custom Microsoft Entra directory roles named Approver and Viewer
Define Approver and Viewer app roles and assign users or groups to them in the enterprise application
Assign custom security attributes named Approver and Viewer to users

explanation: App roles are defined on the app registration, assigned to users or groups through the enterprise application, and emitted in the roles claim of the token. A groups claim can work but ties the app to group IDs and is not managed as roles on the enterprise application. Directory roles grant permissions in Microsoft Entra ID, not inside an app. Custom security attributes are not included in tokens.

prompt: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys resources to Azure by using an app registration. Security wants no client secrets or certificates stored in GitHub. What should be configured on the app registration?

options.text: A federated identity credential trusting GitHub tokens for the repository and branch
A client secret with a 30-day expiry stored as an encrypted GitHub Actions repository secret
A certificate credential with the private key stored as an encrypted GitHub secret
A system-assigned managed identity on the GitHub-hosted runner

explanation: Workload identity federation lets the app registration trust tokens from GitHub's identity provider for a defined repository and branch or environment, so the workflow obtains Microsoft Entra tokens without any stored secret. A client secret or a certificate's private key would still be stored in GitHub. GitHub-hosted runners are not Azure resources, so they cannot have a system-assigned managed identity.

prompt: A company wants Defender for Cloud Apps cloud discovery to include traffic from managed Windows laptops when users work from home, not only traffic through the corporate firewall. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: A Docker-based log collector that uploads the corporate firewall logs continuously
A snapshot report built from a manually uploaded proxy log
An app connector for Microsoft 365
The Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration with Defender for Cloud Apps

explanation: The Defender for Endpoint integration feeds cloud discovery from onboarded devices wherever they are, including off the corporate network. A log collector and a snapshot report both depend on firewall or proxy logs, which miss traffic that does not cross the corporate network. An app connector gives API visibility into a sanctioned app but does not discover other apps.

prompt: Compliance wants apps that lack SOC 2 and data-at-rest encryption to receive lower risk scores across the whole cloud app catalog for the organisation. What should the administrator do in Defender for Cloud Apps?

options.text: Override the app score for each discovered app that lacks SOC 2 or encryption at rest
Raise the importance of those risk factors in the Cloud Discovery score metrics settings
Submit a request score update for each affected app
Create a custom app tag named Non-compliant and apply it to the affected apps

explanation: Score metrics let administrators change the weight of individual risk factors and categories so scores are recalculated across the catalog for the organisation. Overriding the app score changes one app at a time and does not alter the scoring logic. Requesting a score update asks Microsoft to review an app's data. A tag labels apps but does not affect their scores.

prompt: Users may use a third-party CRM app from unmanaged devices, but they must not be able to download files from it on those devices. The app is integrated with Microsoft Entra ID for SSO. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Conditional Access App Control for the app, with a session policy that blocks downloads on unmanaged devices
A Defender for Cloud Apps access policy that blocks the CRM app for all sessions from unmanaged devices
A Conditional Access policy for the app that uses the Use app enforced restrictions session control
A file policy on an app connector for the CRM app that quarantines files shared externally

explanation: Conditional Access app control routes the session through Defender for Cloud Apps, where a session policy can block downloads while still allowing use of the app. An access policy would block the whole app, which goes beyond the requirement. App-enforced restrictions are honoured only by apps that support them, such as SharePoint Online and Exchange Online. A file policy scans files at rest through the API and does not stop downloads in real time.

prompt: A company wants users on unmanaged devices to have browser-only access to SharePoint Online with no download, print or sync, using SharePoint's own controls rather than routing sessions through a reverse proxy. What should the administrator configure in Conditional Access?

options.text: The Use Conditional Access App Control session control with the Block downloads option selected
A grant control that requires the device to be marked as compliant in Microsoft Intune
The Use app enforced restrictions session control, with SharePoint set to limited web-only access
A sign-in frequency session control of one hour for SharePoint Online

explanation: App-enforced restrictions pass device information to SharePoint Online, which then enforces its limited web-only experience on unmanaged devices. Conditional Access App Control would route the session through the Defender for Cloud Apps reverse proxy, which the scenario rules out. Requiring a compliant device blocks unmanaged devices completely. Sign-in frequency controls reauthentication, not downloads.

prompt: Security wants an alert, and automatic disabling of the app, whenever an OAuth app registered in the last seven days is granted highly privileged Microsoft Graph permissions. What should the administrator create?

options.text: A Defender for Cloud Apps session policy for Microsoft Graph that blocks high-privilege requests
A user consent setting of Do not allow user consent for any application
An anomaly detection policy in Cloud Discovery for newly discovered apps
An app governance policy from the New highly privileged app template with Disable app

explanation: App governance policies for Microsoft 365 OAuth apps include a New highly privileged app template that checks registration age and powerful permissions, and the policy can disable apps automatically. Session policies act on user sessions in apps routed through Conditional Access app control, not on OAuth apps. Blocking user consent does not stop administrators granting permissions and does not alert. Cloud Discovery anomaly policies analyse traffic logs, not OAuth app permissions.

prompt: Guest users from partners are invited only through access packages. When a guest's last access package assignment ends, the company wants the guest blocked from signing in at once and the guest account deleted 14 days later. Where should the administrator configure this?

options.text: In an access review of all guest users that is set to auto-apply results
In the entitlement management Lifecycle of external users settings
In the External collaboration settings, under guest user access restrictions
In a Conditional Access policy for guests with a 14-day sign-in frequency

explanation: Entitlement management's Lifecycle of external users settings control whether governed guests are blocked from sign-in and removed when they lose their last access package assignment, and how many days pass before removal. An access review removes access only when a review runs and is not triggered by the last assignment ending. Guest user access restrictions control what guests can see in the directory. Sign-in frequency forces reauthentication and does not block or delete accounts.

prompt: A company wants any user from a partner's Microsoft Entra tenant to be able to request an access package from the My Access portal, without inviting each user first, while users from other organisations cannot request it. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: Cross-tenant synchronization from the partner tenant into the company tenant
B2B direct connect inbound access for the partner tenant
A connected organization for the partner, used in a policy for users not in the directory
An access package policy for users in your directory, after bulk inviting all the partner's users as guests

explanation: A connected organization represents the partner's tenant or domain, and an access package policy for users not in your directory can be limited to specific connected organizations, so only that partner's users can request access. Cross-tenant synchronization is for tenants within the same organisation and creates accounts in advance. B2B direct connect is used for Teams shared channels and does not support access package requests. Bulk inviting everyone first is the manual work the company wants to avoid.

prompt: Guests must accept a non-disclosure agreement before using a project SharePoint site, and they must accept it again every 90 days. The administrator has created a terms of use and a Conditional Access policy that requires it for guests. What else should be configured?

options.text: Set Duration before re-acceptance required (days) to 90 on the terms of use
Set a sign-in frequency of 90 days in the Conditional Access policy that requires the terms
Create an access review of guest users that recurs every 90 days
Set the access package assignment expiration to 90 days

explanation: The terms of use setting Duration before re-acceptance required (days) makes each user accept the terms again after the specified number of days. Sign-in frequency forces reauthentication but does not prompt for the terms again. An access review recertifies access but does not collect a new acceptance. Access package expiration ends access entirely instead of asking for re-acceptance.

prompt: The Marketing manager should be able to create and manage access packages that contain only Marketing groups and sites, without permission to manage other departments' access packages. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Assign the manager the Identity Governance Administrator role
Assign the manager the Groups Administrator role in an administrative unit for Marketing
Make the manager an access package assignment manager for all access packages in the General catalog
Create a Marketing catalog with the Marketing resources and make the manager its owner

explanation: Catalog owners manage the resources and access packages within their own catalog, which delegates entitlement management for one department. Identity Governance Administrator manages entitlement management tenant wide. Groups Administrator in an administrative unit manages groups but not access packages. Access package assignment managers can only manage assignments, not create access packages.

prompt: Users who hold the Payables Clerk access package must not be able to obtain the Payment Approver access package, to keep separation of duties. How should the administrator enforce this?

options.text: Require two-stage approval, with a finance manager as the second approver, in the Payment Approver policy
Mark Payables Clerk as an incompatible access package on Payment Approver
Create an access review of the Payment Approver access package each month
Place both access packages in different catalogs

explanation: Incompatible access packages and groups in the separation of duties settings stop users who already have one access package from requesting the other. Multi-stage approval adds oversight but approvers could still approve the conflicting request. A monthly review only finds conflicts after access has been granted. Placing the packages in different catalogs does not prevent anyone holding both.

prompt: An administrator wants an access review of users assigned to a SaaS application to show reviewers only the users who have not signed in to the tenant for at least 60 days. How should the review be configured?

options.text: Select Inactive users (on tenant level) only and set the days inactive to 60
Scope the review to guest users only and turn on reviewer decision helper recommendations
Set the review recurrence to every 60 days
Set If reviewers don't respond to Remove access

explanation: The inactive users option limits the review to users with no interactive or non-interactive sign-in for the chosen number of days. Scoping to guests excludes members, and recommendations only advise reviewers. A 60-day recurrence changes how often the review runs, not who is in it. The no-response setting decides what happens to undecided users and does not filter the list.

prompt: For a sensitive finance group, users' managers must review membership first, and the group owners must then make the final decision only for users that managers approved. What should the administrator create?

options.text: Two separate single-stage access reviews running at the same time
A single-stage review with managers as reviewers and the group owners configured as fallback reviewers
A multi-stage review with managers first and group owners second, passing on only approved users
A self-review where each member justifies their own access

explanation: Multi-stage reviews run stages in sequence and can pass only users approved in the earlier stage to later reviewers. Two parallel reviews do not chain decisions. Fallback reviewers act only when the primary reviewer cannot be found, such as a user with no manager. Self-review lets users attest their own access, which is weaker oversight than the requirement.

prompt: A company wants one recurring access review that covers guest users in every Microsoft 365 group in the tenant, including groups created later. How should the review scope be set?

options.text: Teams + Groups, with the groups selected individually and All users as the user scope
Applications, with every Microsoft 365 app selected and guest users only
Microsoft Entra roles, with the Guest Inviter role selected
Teams + Groups, with All Microsoft 365 groups with guest users and Guest users only

explanation: Selecting all Microsoft 365 groups with guest users and the guest-only user scope creates a review that covers every such group, including ones added later. Picking groups individually misses future groups and includes members. Reviewing applications does not cover group membership. Reviewing the Guest Inviter role covers role holders, not guests in groups.

prompt: Auditors require that, at the end of each quarterly access review of an application, any user that reviewers did not act on loses access automatically, without an administrator doing anything. Which two settings should be configured?

options.text: Auto apply results to resource
If reviewers don't respond set to Remove access
If reviewers don't respond set to Take recommendations
Send reminders to reviewers
Require reason on approval

explanation: Auto apply results applies the outcomes when the review ends, and setting the no-response behaviour to Remove access denies users with no decision. Take recommendations would keep users the system recommends approving. Reminders and requiring a reason improve reviewer participation and records but do not remove access.

prompt: An access review of a security group has completed. It was not configured to auto-apply results, and reviewers denied access for 12 members. What should the administrator do to remove those members?

options.text: Delete the access review so its decisions take effect
Open the completed review instance and select Apply to apply the results
Create a new access review with auto-apply enabled and wait for it to finish
Run a bulk remove members operation using the list of all current group members

explanation: When auto-apply is off, an administrator can apply the decisions of a completed review manually with Apply, which removes the denied users. Deleting a review discards it without changing membership. A new review delays the change and asks reviewers to repeat their work. Removing all current members would also remove the users who were approved.

prompt: A company is creating emergency access accounts so it can regain administrative access if the federation service or normal administrator MFA fails. Which configuration follows Microsoft guidance?

options.text: Two accounts synchronized from on-premises Active Directory, each with an eligible PIM assignment to Global Administrator that needs MFA on activation
One account with an eligible Global Administrator assignment that requires approval from the security team
Two cloud-only onmicrosoft.com accounts with permanent Global Administrator, passkeys, and sign-in alerts
One cloud-only account that uses SMS for MFA and is excluded from sign-in monitoring and alerting to reduce noise

explanation: Emergency access accounts should be cloud-only so they do not depend on on-premises or federated systems, be permanently assigned so activation or approval cannot block them, use strong phishing-resistant authentication, and be monitored for any sign-in. Synchronized accounts depend on on-premises infrastructure. An approval requirement can make the account unusable in a crisis. SMS is a weak method and sign-ins to these accounts must always be alerted.

prompt: Membership of a security group grants Contributor access to several Azure subscriptions and access to a SaaS app. Engineers should become members only for a few hours when needed, with justification. What should the administrator configure?

options.text: PIM for Groups with engineers as eligible members who must give a justification
A dynamic membership rule that adds engineers to the group
An access package with a 365-day assignment duration that contains the group as its resource
A Conditional Access policy that requires MFA for the SaaS app

explanation: PIM for Groups makes users eligible for group membership or ownership and lets them activate it just in time for a limited duration with justification, which carries all the group's access. A dynamic rule grants standing membership. A 365-day assignment is long-lived access, not just-in-time. Conditional Access requires MFA but does not limit when users hold access.

prompt: A company wants everyone who needs the Owner role on a production Azure subscription to be eligible rather than permanently assigned, and to require MFA and approval on activation. Which role must the administrator hold on the subscription to configure this in PIM, at a minimum?

options.text: Contributor
Privileged Role Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID
User Access Administrator
Security Administrator in Microsoft Entra ID

explanation: Managing PIM for Azure resource roles requires a role that can manage role assignments on the resource, such as Owner or User Access Administrator, and User Access Administrator is the less privileged of the two. Contributor cannot manage role assignments. Privileged Role Administrator and Security Administrator are Microsoft Entra roles and do not grant rights over Azure resource role assignments.

prompt: An administrator configures the Exchange Administrator role in PIM to require approval on activation but does not select any specific approvers. Who will receive and approve activation requests?

options.text: The requester's manager
Members of the Exchange Administrator role who are already active
Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators
No one, so requests are approved automatically

explanation: If approval is required and no approvers are chosen, Privileged Role Administrators and Global Administrators become the default approvers. PIM does not route Microsoft Entra role approvals to managers or to other holders of the same role by default. Requiring approval never results in automatic approval.

prompt: During an investigation, a security analyst needs a list of who activated or was assigned Microsoft Entra roles through PIM over the last few weeks, including activation justifications. Where should the analyst look first?

options.text: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs filtered by the Azure portal application
The resource audit in PIM for Microsoft Entra roles
The Identity Secure Score improvement actions
The access reviews history report

explanation: PIM's resource audit for Microsoft Entra roles lists activations, assignments and other PIM actions with details such as the requester and justification. Sign-in logs record authentication, not role activation. Identity Secure Score lists posture recommendations. Access review history covers review decisions, not role activations.

prompt: A company must query Microsoft Entra sign-in and audit logs with KQL and use Microsoft Entra workbooks, and it must also keep a copy of the logs for two years at the lowest cost for compliance. Which two diagnostic settings destinations should the administrator configure?

options.text: A Log Analytics workspace
An Azure Event Hubs namespace
An Azure storage account
A Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps log collector
An Azure SQL database

explanation: Sending logs to a Log Analytics workspace enables KQL queries and Microsoft Entra workbooks, and archiving to a storage account is the low-cost option for long-term retention. Event Hubs streams logs to SIEM or other external tools and does not store them long term. A Defender for Cloud Apps log collector ingests firewall logs for discovery. Azure SQL is not a diagnostic settings destination.

prompt: Microsoft Entra logs are sent to a Log Analytics workspace. An administrator needs a KQL query that shows which Azure resources' managed identities signed in and to which resources they requested tokens. Which table should the query use?

options.text: SigninLogs
AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs
AuditLogs
AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs

explanation: Managed identity sign-ins are written to the AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs table when that log category is exported. SigninLogs holds interactive user sign-ins, and AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs holds sign-ins that clients perform on behalf of users. AuditLogs records directory changes, not sign-ins.

prompt: Before blocking legacy authentication, an administrator wants a visual report of which users and applications still sign in with legacy protocols such as POP, IMAP and older Exchange ActiveSync clients. Microsoft Entra logs are already sent to Log Analytics. What should the administrator use?

options.text: The Sign-ins using legacy authentication workbook
The provisioning logs filtered by status
The Identity Secure Score page
The audit logs filtered by the Core Directory service

explanation: The Sign-ins using legacy authentication workbook summarises legacy protocol sign-ins by user, app and protocol from data in Log Analytics. Provisioning logs show account provisioning to apps, not sign-ins. Identity Secure Score recommends blocking legacy authentication but does not list who uses it. Audit logs record configuration changes, not sign-in protocols.

prompt: A company uses a third-party product to enforce a control that an Identity Secure Score improvement action recommends. The administrator wants the score to give credit for that control. What should the administrator do?

options.text: Set the improvement action status to Risk accepted
Set the improvement action status to Resolved through third party
Set the improvement action status to Planned
Wait for the next daily recalculation without changing the action

explanation: Marking an improvement action as Resolved through third party awards its points because the control is met by a non-Microsoft product. Risk accepted removes the action from the list without awarding points. Planned records intent and awards nothing. The daily recalculation evaluates only Microsoft configuration and cannot detect the third-party control.

prompt: Automatic user provisioning to a SaaS application is configured, and one new hire never received an account in the app. The administrator needs to see whether the provisioning service skipped the user or the app rejected the create request, and why. What should the administrator review?

options.text: The Microsoft Entra sign-in logs for the new hire
The audit logs filtered by the User Management category and the new hire's name
The provisioning logs for the application, filtered by the new hire's identity
The Usage and insights report for the application

explanation: Provisioning logs record each action the provisioning service takes for an app, including skipped users and errors returned by the target app with their reasons. Sign-in logs show authentication attempts, which a user without an account may never make. Audit logs record directory changes, not the provisioning service's actions in the target app. Usage and insights shows sign-in activity to apps.
